reason: The v0.3.1 edge-split result establishes that every categorical tree has at least one realizable one-transition state with rho at or above 0.15. This rules out a hard one-transition upper ceiling below the benchmark, but maximum >= benchmark does not by itself prove that a state exists within the benchmark calibration tolerance.
supported_claims: All 276 categorical trees contain at least one realizable one-transition edge-split state with rho >= 0.15.
All 220 original OU no-bracket systems contain at least one such state.
The observed OU calibration failure cannot be attributed to a hard one-transition state-space ceiling below 0.15.
The edge-split witness is a one-sided structural ceiling diagnostic, not proof of exact per-tree target attainability.
unsupported_claims_to_avoid: rho = 0.15 is exactly structurally realizable on every tree
every tree contains a state within the frozen rho tolerance around 0.15
the edge-split maximum alone proves exact target assignability
manuscript_rule: Use 'structural feasibility' as the general framework gate. Describe the empirical v0.3.1 implementation as a one-sided structural ceiling/witness test that excludes a hard ceiling below the target. Reserve 'target assignment' for generator calibration that actually brackets the frozen target.
